title: Multi-environment escalation and rollback protocol for model rollout regressions
creator: Alexandra Chen
description:
Purpose:
Create a pragmatic, triage-first playbook for Model Rollout Regressions that occur across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments. This ticket captures a single-source runbook tailored to:
- quickly identify whether a regression is infrastructure, model, or config-induced,
- coordinate cross-team rollback or mitigation steps (hosted fallbacks, dedicated pool draining, private control-plane guidance), and
- standardize customer communication during escalations so SLA-bearing customers get timely updates.

Scope:
- Canary and canary-failure detection signals for all three environments.
- Decision gates for automatic vs. manual rollback.
- Clear handoff/checklist for bridging SRE, Serving Runtime, Customer Success, and Sales for high-severity escalations.
- Post-incident follow-up template and required telemetry to capture for root cause analysis.

Out-of-scope:
- Long-term architectural changes to model selection engine (separate RFC).
acceptance_criteria:
1) On-call can execute the playbook start-to-finish in a simulated canary-failure tabletop test within 60 minutes.
2) Communication templates get approved by Legal and CS for high-impact customers.
3) Playbook includes a matrix mapping observable signals to probable root causes and an ordered rollback decision table.
4) Dashboards and alert thresholds referenced in the playbook are linked and validated.
steps: Initial detection: Verify alerts from runtime-tracing, console-deployment-health, and customer-reported issues. Correlate timestamps across Hosted API logs, Dedicated pool metrics, and Private control-plane audit logs.

Quick triage (first 10 minutes): Determine if symptoms are (a) a complete functional regression (incorrect tokens/format), (b) latency/backpressure, or (c) partial failures (timeouts, increased reject rate). Record observed error codes and sample traces.

Isolate scope (10-20 minutes): Check canary cohort results, model variant differences, and traffic routing rules. Use synthetic test queries (from /infra/playbooks/synthetic-tests) to reproduce failure across environments.

Decision gate A (20-30 minutes): If model functional regression confirmed in canary and affects Hosted or Dedicated with <5% traffic, trigger automated throttling to 0 for that variant. For Private deployments, advise customer ops and provide rollback commands but only proceed with customer approval unless customer has delegated rollback authority.

Mitigation (30-60 minutes): If automated throttling insufficient or regression expands, execute staged rollback: Hosted -> immediate rollback to last-stable model-tag and enable prefix KV caching preservation; Dedicated -> drain affected GPU pools and remap routes to compatible variant; Private -> provide signed rollback script and coordinate with customer SRE with 1-hour priority window.

Customer communication (concurrent): Post initial incident notification to affected customers within 15 minutes. Update every 30 minutes with status, ETA for mitigation, and recommended temporary workarounds (e.g., fallback endpoints, reduced batch size).

Post-rollback validation: Run deterministic prompt set and monitoring checks for 45 minutes across regions. Re-open canary once stability metrics (error-rate < baseline+2sd, P99 latency within SLO) hold for 30 minutes.

Post-incident follow-up: Create incident ticket with timeline, attach traces, include hypothesis and experiments run. Schedule a 72-hour follow-up with Customer Success for any compensations or billing adjustments.
communication_templates: Initial customer notification: 'We have detected a model behavior regression impacting [product area]. Our on-call team is investigating. Your requests may see degraded outputs or increased latency. We will provide an update within 15 minutes and a mitigation ETA within 60 minutes. Incident ID: [ENG-9759]. Contact: escalation@redwood.ai.'

Rollback confirmation: 'We rolled back the model serving for your tenant to the previously validated version ([model-tag]) at [timestamp]. Please validate your critical flows and report any anomalies to support. We will continue monitoring and follow up with a post-incident report.'

Private deployment advisory: 'We have observed a model variant regression during your recent rollout. We recommend running the attached rollback script (signed) or scheduling a guided rollback with Redwood SRE. If you want Redwood to perform the rollback under your delegated runbook, please confirm via secure channel.'

2026-02-18 - Rohit Patel: Added decision gate for Private deployments to respect customer rollback authority. Left placeholder for signed rollback script location.
2026-02-25 - Priya Nair (SRE): Included steps for draining Dedicated GPU pools and notes on KV cache preservation during rollback. Added monitoring thresholds for P99 latency and error rate.

2026-03-07 - QA tabletop: Simulated canary regression. Timeline completed in 48 minutes. Observations: automation gate misfired when metadata mismatch occurred; added metadata validation step.
2026-03-10 - Rohit Patel: Playbook updated with metadata validation, improved rollback script path, and communication cadence. Ready for cross-team review.
resolution_summary: In simulated test the rollback path restored functional outputs for Hosted and Dedicated in under 50 minutes. Private rollback guidance validated with a partner customer who executed the signed script in a pre-scheduled blackout window. Remaining actions: automate metadata validation and add a canary health webhook to console.
